data.name: Ruthenah
data.gender_notes: Ruthenah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Ruthenah means 'red as a rose'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'ruth', meaning 'friend' or 'companion'. In the Bible, Ruth is the name of a Moabite woman who, through her faith and loyalty, became an integral part of the Israelite people. The name Ruthenah is a beautiful reminder of the power of faith and the strength of the bond of friendship.
data.etymology: Ruthenah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red as a rose.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ruthenah total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ruthenah has a rich cultural heritage, combining elements of Jewish, Hebrew, and Biblical origins. It highlights the idea of getting closer to God through companionship, love, and advocacy - virtues that extend beyond ethnic, cultural, and religious lines. It reminds us of the power of unwavering loyalty and the strength of the bonds we forge with those who share our journeys.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ruthenah carries deep spiritual significance, calling to mind the story of Ruth in the Bible. Her tale serves as a powerful reminder of the importance ofconnection, commitment, and faith. As a Ruthenah, one may draw inspiration from Ruth's steadfastness and loyalty, embracing a life firmly anchored in the belief that these virtues will guide and strengthen us. The name is a call to remember the presence and power of God in our daily lives, and to live in accordance with His love and grace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ruthenah, meaning "Redemption" in Hebrew, symbolizes the transformative power of faith in God. It reminds us of the profound restoration that comes through His love and grace, offering hope and renewal in a world of chaos and suffering.
